title: valid-verbs-standard-cli-vocabulary
owner: CC owns the mechanism. Akien owns the verb list and their semantics (get=JSON, show=human-readable, etc.).
intention: A declared vocabulary of standard CLI verbs (get, show, list, ...) that every device implements through its shim, with validation of new commands against the vocabulary and standard shortcuts that compose into the full form.
why: Akien, 2026-08-27: 'we need a list of common verbs new things can't step on. like get should return whatever is asked for, prolly in json format. and show should prolly return the same thing, but formatted for humans, like in chat.' Without a vocabulary, cairn trouble get and cairn tester get could mean different things. Claude is the user — one mental model for all devices.
traces_to: Law 1 — a settled verb vocabulary means new commands don't re-derive what 'get' or 'show' means.
Law 4 — validation against the vocabulary is enforcement by physics (the shim refuses a colliding verb), not policy.
The complexity axis — the root shim class is the base that devices extend; common verbs are the base vocabulary.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. PROVE GATE: the root shim declares verbs, a device inherits them, get returns JSON, show returns human-readable, a colliding verb is refused. FEEDS BACK: a red names which verb or device failed.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when (1) the root shim class declares standard verbs with semantics, (2) devices inherit common handlers, (3) collisions are refused, (4) cairn device get thing works uniformly. WRONG INTENT if the vocabulary is prose, if devices must opt in, or if standard verbs don't compose.
falsifier.horizon: Moderate to large — touches the root shim class, device shims, and cairn command dispatch.

questions.a: ADDRESSING vs ACTION: the-cli-reaches-any-device is the addressing layer (making every device reachable). This is the action layer (what you can DO once you reach a device). They compose.

STANDARD vs DEVICE-SPECIFIC: the standard set is SMALL and reserved (get, show, list). Device-specific verbs are OPEN. The vocabulary governs standard verbs; device verbs are unconstrained beyond not colliding.
LONG FORM vs SHORTCUT: 'cairn device get thing' is the standard; 'cairnhelp' is a shortcut. The vocabulary is the source; shortcuts are views.

how.vocabulary: A data structure in the root shim class mapping verb names to their semantics. RULED 2026-09-06 (Akien, verbatim on the note of that date): the root set is exactly list, show, get, stop, start, settings. get returns JSON, show renders human-readable, list enumerates. `status` is a root view: list/show/get status carry the same content the web STATUS pane carries (shim.active_page: introspect()['intention'] + ['state']). `settings` carries the same content as the web SETTINGS pane (introspect()['settings']) and answers 'No settings' when the device declares none. start/stop act on the device instance's process (a device is its own process in the rack).
how.inheritance: The root shim class implements common verb handlers (get pid, get uptime, list verbs). Devices inherit and can extend with device-specific verbs.
how.dispatch: cairn <device> <verb> <args> → device shim's verb handler. Extends the COMPOSING_DOOR pattern (commit a9e1943).
how.validation: A verb that collides with a standard one is refused at registration time (Law 4).
how.composability: cairnhelp = cairn cairn show help. The long form is the standard; shortcuts are derived, not declared.
how.status_and_settings: CC's reading, not ruled: 'status' and 'settings' resolve through declared_views() so show/get/list already compose over them; `settings` is ALSO a bare verb (`cairn <device> settings`) that renders the settings view and says 'No settings' on an empty dict. The validate berth validate-20260906T111655-4ad94dfa32c8.json predates this ruling and covers only `list`; the build follows the ticket.
how.modifiers: Akien, 2026-09-06: `hot` — a modifier on show/get/list: "don't show cached values, get the real values." Verbatim: "lets say i type 'cairn librarian show status hot' ... 'hot' isn't in there yet. I added that just now. hot would mean don't show cached values, get the real values." A hot query requires the device to be running, so the shim's resolver starts the device (lazy init) before answering; without `hot`, the shim answers from what it holds (last_known / the cached view).
